references.text: Isaac said that Rebekah was his sister because he feared for his life - the direct background to Abimelech's confrontation.
Abram asked Sarai to say she was his sister because he feared for his life, a pattern repeated with Isaac and Rebekah.
Abraham told Abimelech that Sarah was his sister, directly parallel to Isaac's lie to the same king in Gerar.
Abimelech confronted Abraham about his lie, just as he here confronts Isaac - both times with justified indignation.
Fear of people leads to a trap - Isaac's fear of dying led him to lie about his wife.
God's warning to Abimelech about danger to life in the Abraham story explains his concern and confrontation in Isaac's time.
Abimelech's direct question to Abraham mirrors exactly the confrontation he later has with Isaac.
Abimelech's accusation against Abraham of bringing sin upon the kingdom is a direct parallel to the situation with Isaac.
Abraham's original instruction is the direct precursor to Isaac's repetition of the same lie.
